Evidence, re-verified: the filed Problem holds at this tree. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:workspaces_plan lists WS_PROFILE (.ok-workspaces/config.json, converge:1208) under WS_RETIRED_TOPS (converge:1213); at converge:1543 a file whose top name is in that list becomes a removal candidate, and converge:1550-1554 sends it to plan["removes"] unless it carries uncommitted changes or sits behind a symbolic link. A committed, hand-edited profile is removed by git rm (converge:552 prints "removed: <path> (git rm; staged)") with no offer. The profile stays only while a kept port-block or an outside run-tag path reads it (keep_profile, converge:1537). The product's own administration document already states this: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md:197, "The profile, config.proposed.json, LICENSE, ... go, with git rm where git tracks them, so each is recoverable. One that carries uncommitted changes or sits behind a symbolic link is an estate-edits offer instead."

Mechanism: the workspaces migration judges "owner content" only by git state (uncommitted or symlinked), never by content. The plumbline migration in the same core offers any file it does not recognize as an estate-leftover (converge:1290, leftover_offer) and any unstamped suite file as estate-edits, and it carries a config-conflict offer for its config (converge:1319). The profile was written by the retired family's resolve as transcription of the owner's answers, and the owner may add keys by hand.

Corpus: decision:whole-file-ownership says "the suite's own retired-layout content is suite territory, migrated mechanically under the administration's own authorization", and also "owner-declared configuration ... is written only as transcription of explicit answers" and "anything else at a path the suite cares about ... is presented for the owner's decision". It does not say whether a retired estate's owner-declared configuration is retired-layout content. decision:administration-is-a-user-act reserves consent "for content the suite does not own, and for transcription into owner-declared configuration". story:converge-project-estate promises "upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote"; git history keeps the file, so whether a recoverable git rm costs the owner work is the reading in dispute.

Harm: an owner key in a committed profile leaves the working tree with only a "removed:" line as notice. No accept-list entry needs to cover a judgment issue; A2 (cleanup reaches something it did not create) is the nearest, and its weight is reduced because git rm keeps the file recoverable.

Options:
1. Amend story:converge-project-estate (or decision:whole-file-ownership) to say converge removes a retired estate's owner-declared configuration whole, recoverable from version history, and names each file in its report. Cost: no code change; an owner's hand-added keys leave silently except for the report line; ADMINISTRATION.md:197 already matches.
2. Amend decision:whole-file-ownership to say owner-declared configuration in a retired estate, edited or not, reaches the owner as a cleanup offer before converge removes it. Cost: a code change in workspaces_plan (the profile becomes an estate-leftover or estate-edits offer), an ADMINISTRATION.md change, and one more question on every legacy project's first converge, which the decision's Alternatives warn against ("stalls every legacy project's first converge on a question with one sensible answer").
3. Missed by the filer: offer the profile only when it holds content beyond what the retired resolve would write (keys the suite never wrote, or values that differ from the defaults), and remove a profile the suite could regenerate. Cost: the core must carry the retired profile's schema to compare against; the corpus still needs a sentence saying edited owner configuration in a retired estate is offered.

Siblings: rule with administration-doc-omits-converge-refusals-and-offer-scope (same ADMINISTRATION.md workspaces section) and drivers-ran-the-converge-core-on-the-live-repository (the same core's migration of .ok-workspaces/).

Evidence, re-verified: README.md still describes the three-family suite. README.md:9 'The marketplace distributes exactly two user-scoped plugins' while .claude-plugin/marketplace.json lists ok, ok-conduct, and ok-web; README.md:11 and :19 speak of 'skill families' and per-family administration; README.md:48-49 list ok-plumbline and ok-workspaces rows; README.md:63-67 name /patterns and /budget; README.md:175 names plugins/ok/families/{ok-planner,ok-plumbline,ok-workspaces}, where plugins/ok/families/ now holds ok-planner alone. The filed line numbers hold. README.md carries no /document provenance stamp, and no document type exists: .ok-planner/surface/documents/ is absent. Mechanism: no work item and no document type claims README.md, and the converge fix loop bars fixers from prose (.claude/skills/converge/prompts/fix.md, verify.md), so the round-1 rewrite was sent back and the file is back at base 9c7aff7. Corpus: decision:documents-generated-per-type-and-placed says 'Only declared types' targets are written; a project that keeps a hand-written root readme declares no type targeting it.' So today README.md is a hand-written owner file. decision:placed-documents-are-records governs only a document the ceremony placed, with a stamp; README.md is not one. decision:one-vendored-family is the ruling the README contradicts. Harm: A9 reads on it loosely (an entry document tells a user which verbs and families install, and that is not so), but the filer offers the owner a choice of who maintains the file, so it is a judgment issue. Options: (1) the owner revises README.md by hand before the next release; cost: hand-kept prose drifts again at the next consolidation, and nothing notices. (2) Declare a document type targeting README.md, so each /document release revises it; cost: README.md becomes a placed record under decision:placed-documents-are-records, regenerated from the audit and out of agent context, and the owner gives up hand tuning. (3) A follow-up sprint carries a work item that rewrites README.md for the one-family suite; cost: a sprint for a prose fix, and the file stays hand-kept afterward. Options 1 and 3 can pair with option 2 later. Siblings: fix-loop-cannot-fix-prose-sites (why the converge loop could not fix it), contract-licenses-a-retired-payload-class and administration-doc-omits-converge-refusals-and-offer-scope (the same prose-in-product-tree gap).

Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/catalog-toc (materialized as .ok-planner/bin/catalog-toc) regenerates only subjects.md and practices.md: its CATALOGS tuple names ('subjects', ...) and ('practices', ...) and nothing else, and --check covers only those two. The design TOCs are written by an agent: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md:61, step 7, tells the agent to read every file under concepts/, stories/, decisions/ and write concepts.md, stories.md, decisions.md by hand; the sprint build instructions (skills/_sprint/shared.md:148, plan-sprint/SKILL.md:98, _shared/artifact-definitions.md:164) run catalog-toc only for subject and practice deltas. The design TOCs match their catalogs today (35 concepts, 23 stories, 50 decisions, bullet for bullet); the filed drift (a stale completion-report row) was before the sprint applied its deltas. Mechanism: the sprint amended decision:generated-catalog-tocs and dropped its sentence 'The periodic audit and the certification gate check each table of contents ... neither is the generator', so no backstop names design-TOC staleness in the decision now; the design-doc compliance reviewer (_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md:172, 'TOC consistency') still checks it, and concept:catalog-toc Boundaries says 'Checking TOC consistency ... belongs to the corpus audit'. Corpus: decision:generated-catalog-tocs Choice, 'Every durable catalog in an estate carries a table of contents beside it, and a generator writes that file from the catalog's own artifacts. Nobody edits a table of contents by hand'; concept:catalog-toc, 'the generated one-file index beside each durable catalog'. Neither says whether an agent following a fixed procedure counts as a generator. Harm: none an accept-list entry names today; a hand-written TOC can drift from its catalog, and every session reads it first. Options: (1) amend the decision to say one generator script writes every catalog's TOC, the design catalogs included, and extend catalog-toc to concepts/stories/decisions with their per-kind summary rules (discover-design step 7 already states them); cost: a script change and its summary heuristics for three more kinds, and discover-design step 7 and the sprint build steps change to run the script. (2) Amend the decision to say a script writes the subject and practice TOCs and an agent following a fixed procedure writes the design TOCs; cost: 'Nobody edits a table of contents by hand' needs rewording, and design-TOC drift stays possible with only the compliance reviewer and the audit to notice. (3) Leave the decision as written and read 'generator' as mechanical, making option 1's script work a remediation item with no corpus change; cost: the owner must accept that the current procedure breaks the decision until a sprint builds it. No sibling issue.

Evidence, re-verified: decision:lockstep-suite-version Choice ends 'The conduct's version is the one carve-out: hand-managed and untouched by a release, which warns when the conduct's body changed without a bump and does nothing further', and Rationale says 'A warning keeps the conduct's number its author's to set'. The sprint's staged amendment of this decision kept both sentences. .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md step 4 (lines 97-122), 'Bump the conduct version when the conduct body changed', says 'the release owns it, exactly as it owns the plugin manifests. Nobody hand-edits the stamp', and advances the minor and the animal mechanically; SKILL.md:32 lists the conduct stamp as release-mutable metadata and SKILL.md:212 repeats it. plugins/ok-conduct/CLAUDE.md:16 agrees with the release skill: the stamp is 'owned by the repo-root /release skill ... Never hand-edit it'. History: the carve-out sentence entered the decision at a519393 (Release v9.0.0); 'Nobody hand-edits the stamp' entered the release skill at a15d4e8 (Release v18.5.1, 2026-08-15); the decision was edited again at 2718095 (2026-08-21) and by the sprint, both keeping the carve-out. The design/_discover notes still describe the old warn-only behavior. Mechanism: the release skill is project-local tooling (no Materialized stamp; it says it is not part of any distributed plugin), so the change is the project's own, and the decision is a live corpus commitment; one of the two must change. Corpus: decision:lockstep-suite-version is the only artifact that speaks to it; concept:conduct is silent on who sets the number. Harm: no accept-list entry; a reader of the corpus expects a release never to touch the conduct stamp, and /release rewrites it. Options: (1) amend decision:lockstep-suite-version so a release bumps the conduct's stamp when the conduct's body changed and the stamp did not move, keeping an author-landed conduct-major; this matches the release skill and plugins/ok-conduct/CLAUDE.md:16 and the behavior every release since v18.5.1 has run; cost: the Choice's clause 'it changes only release-mutable metadata — the manifest version fields and the stamps a re-converge rewrites' must also name the conduct stamp, and the Rationale's warning sentence goes. (2) Edit release skill step 4 to warn on a changed conduct body under an unchanged stamp and leave the stamp to its author, and edit plugins/ok-conduct/CLAUDE.md:16 to match; cost: the author must remember to bump by hand, which the v18.5.1 change was made to remove. No sibling issue.

Stuck in converge-2026-10-04T060800, so a judgment issue. Evidence, re-verified: docs/integration-contract.md:262-266, section Support scripts, still reads 'Exactly two classes legitimately run from the carried payload: the administration process itself (diagnosis, bootstrap, and converge run before or while the project copies are being written), and read-only advisory verbs falling back with an announcement in their output.' The backout restored the build's two-class sentence; the harm stands. No skill under plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills or plugins/ok/skills falls back to the payload today. docs/integration-contract.md carries no Materialized stamp and no /document provenance stamp, so it is the project's own normative prose, not suite-owned and not a placed record. Corpus: decision:per-project-pinning Choice, 'Exactly one class legitimately runs from the payload: the administration process itself — diagnosis, bootstrap, and converge'; its Alternatives list 'Let read-only verbs fall back to the payload copy and announce it' as rejected. concept:integration-contract names the contract the suite's normative spine. The corpus decides the end state: one class. Harm: A8 reads on it (a live design commitment leaves one compliant sentence), but the only fix is a prose edit the converge prompts bar. Options, from the stuck section: (1) round 1, fix task t31, changed the sentence to 'Exactly one class legitimately runs from the carried payload: the administration process itself', matching decision:per-project-pinning; verify task t37 sent it back: 'change edits prose file docs/integration-contract.md, barred to fixers'. (2) Round 2, fix task t43, made no change and closed blocked; no verifier ran. Fixes no run has tried: (3) the owner makes the round-1 edit by hand, outside the loop; cost: none beyond the owner's time, and the loop's prose bar stays. (4) The next sprint carries a work item rewriting the Support scripts section; cost: a sprint item for one sentence. (5) Change the converge prompts so a fixer may edit product-tree prose where the defect's site is that file (issue fix-loop-cannot-fix-prose-sites); cost: a tooling change to fix.md and verify.md, suite-owned files, so it goes upstream. Siblings: fix-loop-cannot-fix-prose-sites, readme-describes-the-retired-suite, administration-doc-omits-converge-refusals-and-offer-scope.

Evidence, re-verified: .ok-planner/design/decisions/task-tools-mirror-the-report.md:16, Choice, 'The `execute-tasks` drain marks the entry for a task's key as it dispatches and closes the task, where the caller keeps one.' The payload carries no execute-tasks skill: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ holds _tasks/drain.md and no execute-tasks folder, and the vendored .claude/skills/execute-tasks/ is deleted in the tree. plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md:99 and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md:240 list execute-tasks among the retired names, replaced by 'the drain loop, which /audit, /converge, /triage-issues, and sprint execution read by path'. This decision is the only live corpus artifact that still names execute-tasks. Mechanism: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_tasks/drain.md:24 does the marking now: 'Where the caller keeps a progress checklist in the harness task tools, mark the entry for a task's key in progress when its agent claims it and done when it closes done.' Corpus: decision:no-execution-engine already names 'a task tracker and a drain loop that every executor runs on'. The corpus contradicts a later ruling: the consolidation sprint retired /execute-tasks and moved the loop to _tasks/drain.md, and decision:one-vendored-family is that sprint's ruling. Harm: no accept-list entry beyond a live decision naming a verb that no longer exists; the filed 'C4' is not on the accept list. The one compliant corpus change: replace 'The `execute-tasks` drain' with 'The drain loop' (the loop at .claude/skills/_tasks/drain.md), and match the moments drain.md:24 names: it marks the entry in progress when the task's agent claims it and done when the task closes done, where the caller keeps a checklist. No other sentence changes. Sibling: none.

Evidence, re-verified: the filed Problem holds at this tree. Drivers run under the ok-opus profile, and .claude/agents/ok-opus.md:4 reads "disallowedTools: Agent", so a driver cannot run a slash command that dispatches agents (/converge, /converge sprint, /audit). .ok-planner/review/project.md, "What no agent of this loop ever runs", lists /ok. The drive prompt tells the driver to try "the primary surface the project's facts below name first, always" (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/drive.md:23), and project.md names the slash commands as the primary user surface ("Running the product, for the drive"). The merge prompt sorts such a drive as environment ("a need a local stack cannot meet", prompts/merge.md:30). No mechanism skips such a story: project.md's two story lists, "Stories that drive alone" and "Stories that drive on an instance of their own", only order or isolate drivers (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:754-755, cmd_drives:966). review drives already takes --stories (review:974), so a session can file drivers for a subset, but nothing tells it which stories to leave out.

Mechanism: the cheatsheet's Subagent models section says a vendored profile spawns nothing but forks, and only the audit and review profiles fork, so no leaf driver can ever reach an orchestrating surface. Each such story spends a driver and ends at environment with no verdict on its primary surface.

Corpus: decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user says the driver "works out from the running product how to get the benefit on every surface the story is offered through" and that a merge agent sorts a failure "as a failure of the environment"; it is silent on surfaces a driver cannot reach. decision:subagent-model-follows-job and decision:slash-only-activation bear on why a leaf cannot run them. story:find-and-fix-defects, story:certify-completion, story:corpus-audit, story:practice-coverage-report, story:lint-rules-compliance-report, and story:converge-project-estate are the stories affected.

Where the change falls: in this repository the converge skill, its prompts, and the review script are the product's source under plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/ (skills/converge/SKILL.md, skills/converge/prompts/drive.md, scripts/review); their materialized copies under .claude/skills/ and .ok-planner/bin/ are suite-owned and change only through /ok after a release. project.md is the owner's. So options 1 and 2 are sprint work on the product source; option 3 is an owner edit.

Harm: drive runs spend a driver per such story and report no verdict on the story's primary surface. No accept-list entry needs to cover a judgment issue; the environment sort is accurate, so A9 does not hold.

Options:
1. The converge skill skips the drive of a story whose only surface dispatches agents or is forbidden to the loop, and lists it in the return for the owner to drive from a full session. Cost: those six stories are never driven by the loop; decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user ("every surface") likely needs an amendment, and the skill needs a way to know which stories qualify.
2. project.md gains a third list, stories that need a full session, and review drives files drivers only for the rest, reporting the listed ones in the return. Cost: a seeded section, a review script change, and owner upkeep of the list as stories change; it keeps the judgment with the owner rather than the skill.
3. project.md lets a driver run /ok on a scratch copy. Cost: covers only story:converge-project-estate; the driver still cannot dispatch, and /ok updates the operator's installed plugins, which project.md also forbids. It fixes none of the five /converge and /audit stories.
4. Missed by the filer: the session drives such stories itself, in sprint certification or drive mode, since it holds the Agent tool, or drivers drive the stories' non-orchestrating surfaces (the scripts and the converge core) and the return names the primary surface as undriven. Cost: the session's context grows with a nested ceremony, or the primary surface stays unverified by the loop.

Siblings: rule with drive-rule-conflates-no-stack-with-unfilled-commands and drivers-ran-the-converge-core-on-the-live-repository (all three are how the drive meets a product with no stack whose surfaces are slash commands), and with fix-loop-cannot-fix-prose-sites.

EVIDENCE (re-verified). plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:70 (drive mode step 2): where project.md has no `## Drive commands` section "or the section names no command (no `- <role>:` line, as in the seeded skeleton), the drive cannot start". SKILL.md:95 (sprint mode step 4) skips the drive on the same condition. SKILL.md:72 and :107 (stop step, confirm step) file stack-start/stack-stop exec tasks from `review drive-command`, and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:868-878 (cmd_drive_command) raises "gives no line for the role ..." when a role is missing, so a no-stack project also fails the confirm step. This project's .ok-planner/review/project.md has an empty `## Drive commands` section and says under `## Running the product, for the drive`: "The product has no stack to start or stop." The seed at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md:25-31 offers no way to declare "no stack". The filed Problem still holds.
MECHANISM. The skill reads one signal, an empty Drive commands section, for two facts: the owner never filled the section, and the product has no stack. Followed literally, sprint certification skips every drive on a product with no stack.
OWNERSHIP. The change falls in product source in this repo: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, scripts/review, and review/seed/project.md, none of them stamped. The copy at .claude/skills/converge/SKILL.md is suite-owned and follows the next /ok. So this is a question for this repo's /plan-sprint, not an upstream issue.
CORPUS. decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user: "sprint certification does the same for the stories a sprint adds or amends", and a driver "works out from the running product how to get the benefit". That decides the end state: a product with no stack still gets its drive, and only the skeleton skips. The corpus is silent on how project.md declares no stack, so the mechanism is open. The author may write a generated ruling on that end state.
HARM. A drive the sprint requires is skipped, and the return reports "the drive cannot start" for a product that needs no start. Run converge-2026-10-04T060800 departed from the rule by hand (session note i1).
OPTIONS. (1) project.md declares no stack (a marked line in Drive commands, for example a `stack-start` role valued `none`). The skill and `review drive-command` read it, skip the start, stop, and confirm stack tasks, and still file drivers. The skeleton still skips. Cost: a new grammar in the review tool, the skill, and the seed. (2) The seeded project.md gains a no-stack line that `review drive-command` reads and reports. Cost: the seed lands only once, so existing projects edit project.md by hand. (3) Missed by the filer: treat a missing stack-start role as no stack whenever another Drive commands role or the Running section is filled. Cost: it cannot tell the skeleton from no stack when the section is empty, as here, so it needs (1) or (2) anyway. (4) Leave it, and sessions keep departing by hand. Cost: the rule and the decision disagree.

A bare `converge` with no argument still converges the working directory (converge:8, USAGE). The stray converge still stands in the working tree. Under .claude/, vendored skills, agents, hooks, and rules are modified or deleted (for example .claude/agents/ok-sonnet.md, .claude/skills/budget/, and .claude/rules/ok-workspaces-cheatsheet.md, staged). .ok-plumbline/ is staged as renamed or deleted into .ok-planner/ and no longer exists. Of .ok-workspaces/ only bin/ remains. .claude/settings.json:21 still wires `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.ok-plumbline/hooks/post-edit.js"`, a file that is gone. .ok-planner/hooks/post-edit.js exists. So the edit-time lint does not run here. The guard gap stands. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/drive.md:55 says "Edit nothing, stage nothing, commit nothing" and bars git checkout, restore, reset, stash, and clean. It says nothing about running a project script that writes at the project root. In .ok-planner/review/project.md, "What no agent of this loop ever runs" lists `/ok` ("it rewrites the vendored suite layer") but not the converge core, which does the same rewrite. "Resources a driver starts" says to drive the core against a `mktemp -d` scratch folder, and does not put the root off limits. The stall: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:212 takes `fcntl.flock(self.lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)` with no timeout, so a waiter blocks for as long as the holder keeps the lock.
MECHANISM. A driver reads usage by running the script where it stands. The script's default mode writes to the working directory, so a driver at the root rewrites the dogfooded vendored layer.
OWNERSHIP. drive.md's source is product under plugins/ and unstamped. The copy at .claude/skills/converge/prompts/drive.md is suite-owned. project.md is the owner's own file. scripts/tasks is product. Every option is this repo's own change, not upstream.
CORPUS. decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user says a driver "uses only what a user in that role has". The corpus is silent on the project root and on the keep-or-restore choice.
HARM. A driver rewrote the vendored layer that project.md reserves to the owner's /ok. The lint hook now points at a missing file.
OPTIONS. Two separate choices. (A) The working tree, an owner act: (A1) keep the stray converge as this repo's converge to v23.0.0, review its diff, and consent to `converge wire-hooks lint`. Cost: the owner adopts a rewrite nobody reviewed, including the rewrites of the live sprint, .ok-planner/config.json, and .ok-planner/review/config.json. (A2) Restore the vendored layer and the estates from HEAD, then run /ok. Cost: the owner must keep the sprint's own work apart from the stray rewrite, in the same files. (B) A guard, which may combine: (B1) drive.md tells a driver to run every project script against a scratch copy, never at the project root. Cost: a prompt change for every consumer, and a read-only root script such as checks/run also moves to a copy. (B2) project.md names the converge core at the root in "What no agent of this loop ever runs", or names the root off limits in "Resources a driver starts". Cost: none to the suite, and it protects this repo only. (B3) The task tracker gives up a lock wait it cannot win, with an error, at scripts/tasks:212. Cost: a timeout to choose, and a lock-holder that is merely slow now fails. This is separable and could be its own issue.

EVIDENCE (re-verified; all paths are product source under plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/, the .claude/ copies are suite-owned materializations). prompts/fix.md:55 "Leave every prose file, `.claude/`, and `.ok-planner/` untouched". prompts/verify.md:24 "A change that edited a prose file or an estate is sent back whatever else it did." prompts/backout.md:30 "Edit no prose file or estate." prompts/merge.md:43 (step 3a) routes to `judgment` only files under `.claude/`, `.ok-planner/review|bin|hooks|docs|scripts/`, `.ok-planner/design/`, subjects and practices; product prose under plugins/ or docs/ passes 3a and enters the fix loop. SKILL.md:34 "Code only.": the hunt population (`review files`) excludes `.md`, `.markdown`, `.rst`, `.txt`, but sprint mode's review and the drive are not limited to that population, so they still produce prose-site defects. The filed Problem holds.
MECHANISM: the finders can report a prose site, the merge lets it through, and every fixer and verifier is forbidden to change it, so the defect can only end stuck or declined after spending fix rounds.
CORPUS: decision:converge-finds-then-fixes is silent on prose. decision:placed-documents-are-records says "a fixer's restatement sweep ... stop[s] at" placed documents and that a placed document behind the tree files nothing; README.md and docs/integration-contract.md carry no provenance stamp and no document types are declared (.ok-planner/surface/documents/ is absent), so they are not placed documents today, but any option must keep fixers off placed documents. Tooling the change edits: prompts/merge.md, fix.md, verify.md, backout.md, SKILL.md (Code only paragraph), possibly scripts/review and review/seed/config.json for option 3.
HARM: two fix rounds spent on unfixable defects in run converge-2026-10-04T060800 (7 of 9 round-1 fixes sent back for editing `.md`), and the backed-out hunks left ADMINISTRATION.md and the /ok skill describing less than the code (now issue administration-doc-omits-converge-refusals-and-offer-scope, triaged `defect`, whose fix is a prose edit the next /converge cannot make under today's prompts).
OPTIONS: (1) merge.md 3a routes a defect whose only fix is a product-prose edit to `judgment`, so the run spends no fix round. Cost: every prose defect waits for /plan-sprint; in ok-plugins, where most of the product is prose, most defects leave /converge. This is the one change that fits the skill's stated "Code only" rule and fix.md:55 as they stand. (2) fix.md and verify.md let a fixer edit a product prose file where the defect's site is that file, keeping the bar on `.claude/`, the estates, and placed documents. Cost: widens what the loop commits to ("Code only" must change), and verifiers judge prose fixes with no standard beyond the code. (3) review/config.json declares product prose paths, and fix/verify allow edits there alone. Cost: a new config key, seed, and review-tool support; precise and opt-in per project. Options 2 and 3 change what /converge commits to; option 1 does not.

That is why `review changed --help` prints only the usage line. The top-level parser has one description, "the review loop's mechanical steps" (review:1127). review:208-210 (cmd_changed) uses `--sprint` only to add the folders the sprint lists under `## Paths outside the project root` (outside_paths, review:161). The filed Problem holds.
MECHANISM. Through /converge sprint, the owner gets a verdict computed from the recorded base. Someone who runs `review changed --sprint S` by hand gets a diff from HEAD, which is empty once the work is committed, with exit 0 and no warning.
CORPUS. story:certify-completion: "know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered". /converge sprint meets this, and the story names no surface. decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user says a driver works through "the public surface". No surface intent exists (.ok-planner/surface/ is absent), so nothing classes the review tool as public or internal. The corpus does not settle it (call i75).
HARM. A3, if the review tool is a developer or operator script, since project.md lists it: a listed script gives a wrong result (no changes) for a committed sprint. No harm reaches the owner through /converge sprint.
OPTIONS. (1) story:certify-completion states that the owner reaches the delivery verdict through /converge sprint alone, and that the review command line is that ceremony's internal mechanics. Cost: narrows the story, and project.md's operator-script listing should also drop the review tool, or A3 keeps reaching it. (2) story:certify-completion states that the review command line, given a sprint, diffs from the sprint's recorded base and warns when none is recorded. Cost: widens the story, plus a code change in review:cmd_changed (and the checks and snapshot verbs, for one idiom) and help text. (3) Missed by the filer: change no corpus. The owner drops the review tool from project.md's "Scripts for developers and operators" (the owner's own file), so A3 no longer covers it. Cost: the cheapest; leaves a hand user's bare help as it is. (4) Missed by the filer: change no corpus, but give `--sprint` without `--base` the recorded base, or a refusal naming `--base`, and add help text, as a code-only fix. Cost: a review-tool change outside any promise. This only becomes a defect if the owner keeps the tool listed as an operator script.

EVIDENCE (re-verified). plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/port-block:142-152 (recorded_port) refuses only when the record file is missing or does not hold a port number. Otherwise it returns the recorded port, and nothing checks that anything listens on it. port-block:120-139 (service_port) asks docker and refuses with "no running container of service ..." when the compose project has none. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md:146 describes a `record` entry as a dev server "that listens on port 0 and writes the port it got to that path". It says nothing of who removes the record. .ok-planner/review/project.md lists port-block among the scripts for developers and operators. The filed Problem holds: drive failure i28 printed `WEB_PORT=55061` with exit 0 after the server stopped.
MECHANISM. A record file outlives its server unless something deletes it. The operating system may give the freed port to another run's server. A run that reads its stale record back then verifies against that other server.
CORPUS. story:concurrent-stacks-without-port-collisions promises "one verification run never disturbs another's results". decision:os-assigned-ports-read-back-by-run-tag says port-block "reads back, by that tag, the host ports the stack got", and "Where a project's stack cannot bind this way, the project's own stack commands handle isolation". concept:run-tag says "wiring it into builds, stacks, and harnesses is deliberately the project's own change". The decision is silent on a record whose server has stopped. Either reading can cite it: "the ports the stack got" (present tense), or the project's own stack commands. That is call i74.
HARM. A9 would cover it if the decision promises a live readback: a printed result tells the run that its own stack holds a port it does not. Under the other reading, no entry covers it: the trigger needs the project's stack-stop to leave its record behind.
OPTIONS. (1) The decision states that a readback refuses a recorded port nothing listens on, as it refuses a service with no running container. Cost: a liveness probe in recorded_port, which still races (another process can bind the freed port, so the probe sees a listener). It narrows the race and cannot close it, which the decision's own Rationale says of allocators. (2) The decision states that a readback reports what the record holds, and that the project's stack-stop command clears the run's records. Cost: the duty moves to every project's stack commands, and ADMINISTRATION.md's `ports` paragraph and the cheatsheet should say so. (3) Missed by the filer: the record carries the server's process id beside the port, and port-block refuses when that process is gone. Cost: a format change for the record. It ties liveness to the writer rather than to the port, which closes the stale case without the race in (1).
SIBLINGS. review-changed-ignores-the-sprint-base, the other listed-operator-script issue the corpus reads two ways, from the same run.

The profile stays only while a kept port-block or an outside run-tag path reads it (keep_profile, converge:1537). One that carries uncommitted changes or sits behind a symbolic link is an estate-edits offer instead."

Mechanism: the workspaces migration judges "owner content" only by git state (uncommitted or symlinked), never by content. The plumbline migration in the same core offers any file it does not recognize as an estate-leftover (converge:1290, leftover_offer) and any unstamped suite file as estate-edits, and it carries a config-conflict offer for its config (converge:1319). Harm: an owner key in a committed profile leaves the working tree with only a "removed:" line as notice. No accept-list entry needs to cover a judgment issue; A2 (cleanup reaches something it did not create) is the nearest, and its weight is reduced because git rm keeps the file recoverable.

Cost: no code change; an owner's hand-added keys leave silently except for the report line; ADMINISTRATION.md:197 already matches.
2. Amend decision:whole-file-ownership to say owner-declared configuration in a retired estate, edited or not, reaches the owner as a cleanup offer before converge removes it. Cost: a code change in workspaces_plan (the profile becomes an estate-leftover or estate-edits offer), an ADMINISTRATION.md change, and one more question on every legacy project's first converge, which the decision's Alternatives warn against ("stalls every legacy project's first converge on a question with one sensible answer").

Missed by the filer: offer the profile only when it holds content beyond what the retired resolve would write (keys the suite never wrote, or values that differ from the defaults), and remove a profile the suite could regenerate. Cost: the core must carry the retired profile's schema to compare against; the corpus still needs a sentence saying edited owner configuration in a retired estate is offered.

Cost: the duty moves to every project's stack commands, and ADMINISTRATION.md's `ports` paragraph and the cheatsheet should say so. (3) Missed by the filer: the record carries the server's process id beside the port, and port-block refuses when that process is gone. Cost: a format change for the record.
